title: From Far Away I Must Love You
text:
From far away I must love you,

from the quiet distance

where love is nostalgia

and desire is constancy.

From the divine place where

the good of existence

is to be eternity

and to seem absence.

Who needs to explain the moment

and the fragrance of the rose

that persuades without any arrogance?

And at the bottom of the sea the star,

without violence,

fulfills its truth

apart from transparency.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Meireles's distant love as constancy, eternity, and almost absent truth.

title: Motive
text:
I sing because the instant exists

and my life is complete.

I am not joyful and I am not sad:

I am a poet.


Brother of fugitive things,

I feel neither pleasure nor torment.

I cross nights and days

in the wind.


If I crumble or if I build,

if I remain or undo myself,

—I do not know, I do not know. I do not know whether I stay

or pass.


I know that I sing. And the song is everything.

The rhymed wing has eternal blood.

And one day I know I will be mute:

—Nothing more.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Meireles's poised ars poetica: song as everything, and silence as the final limit.

title: Or Outside the World. Why?...
text:
Or outside the world. Why?

But what do I answer him,

If the Archangel asks,

In a deep time?


In the world I was passing:

But very far away.

Through dreams and loves

I was disintegrating.


The world did not see:

My permanence

Was, everywhere,

Phantasmagorical.


I gave, but I did not have.

And in that abundance,

Nothing remained for me:

I do not know whether I was mine.


Whether I was in the world

or outside the world?

—Thus I present myself,

If the Archangel asks

My deep name.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker's uncertain existence between world, dream, abundance, and the Archangel's question.

title: False Map
text:
How many things I thought were sublime,

worthy of abundant tears!

What were they? The tears of memory,

and the pensive plains

through which their long rivers stretched.

But those waters carry no voice.

Everything was drowned and buried.

Greater than the things wept for

were the tears that wept for them.

And at a distance,

their image is a solitude now without meaning,

a false map our journey abandons,

for we always go beyond everything, farther...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's revision of past grief into a map abandoned by the ongoing journey.

title: Childhood
text:
They carried away the balcony railings

from where the house could be seen.

The silver railings.


They carried away the shadow of the lemon trees

through which hoops of music rolled

and reddish ants.


They carried away the house with the green roof

with its shell grottoes

and its stained-glass windows of misted flowers.


They carried away the lady of the old piano

who played, played, played

the pale sonata.


They carried away the eyelids of ancient dreams,

and left only memory

and present tears.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the repeated taking-away of childhood objects until only memory and current tears remain.
